source_cards.title: Beyond Dry References: Learning Relative Audio Effects Representations via Contrastive Distance Learning

method.frontend: log-mel STFT n_fft 2048 hop 512 64 mel bins 50-18000 Hz
method.architecture: weight-shared dual-branch CNN14 with cross-attention differential gating and 128-dimensional projection
training_audio: 6447 mixed tracks / 2681 songs / 185.9 h licensed internal collection
method.pairing: adjacent non-overlapping 10-second clips from the same structural section
method.effect_chain: EQ distortion multiband compressor gain stereo imager limiter delay reverb
method.evaluation: MUSDB18; 100 samples per instrument; seven random restarts; up to 200 iterations; median multi-resolution STFT loss

bounded_findings: relative ordered-pair representations can be trained without a dry reference and improved the paper's objective style-transfer metric under its protocol
same-section cross-segment pairing was central: removing it improved retrieval but degraded style-transfer loss by 34 percent
retrieval accuracy and style-transfer loss can move in opposite directions and are not interchangeable validation targets
the bidirectional variant approximately preserved sign reversal and partial composition in embedding space
limitations: objective multi-resolution STFT loss does not establish production preference
models overall transformations rather than source-specific effects within mixtures
unseen chain orders and real production chains were not evaluated
the training compute and internal licensed collection are not available for project reproduction

source_cards.title: WildFX: A DAW-Powered Pipeline for In-the-Wild Audio FX Graph Modeling

method.renderer: Dockerized REAPER on Linux controlled through reapy/ReaScript
method.graph_scope: acyclic one-sink graphs with constrained sidechains splitters sends gains and layered decomposition
method.compatibility_test: 96 Linux VST3 plugins; loading tests for pedalboard and WildFX; isolated one-second 44.1 kHz 512-sample renders for DawDreamer
method.datasets: two Slakh2100-derived sets, each 5000 train and 270 validation projects
method.estimator_training: four settings trained once for 30000 steps

bounded_findings: the metadata schema explicitly represents plugins parameters gains main/control edges sidechains and graph structure
layered scheduling provides a practical dependency-respecting renderer for the supported DAG subset
the pipeline loaded all 96 tested Linux VST3 plugins whereas the two Python alternatives had failures or silent outputs
the generated data were usable for an initial blind graph-estimation experiment
limitations: plugin loading is not proof of correct or musically meaningful processing
other formats and bridged Windows plugins were not included in the 96-plugin comparison
REAPER headless control has no built-in error reporting and every pipeline step was manually checked in a GUI before deployment
supported graphs are constrained DAGs rather than unrestricted DAW routing
the graph estimator used a five-plugin proof-of-concept inventory, one run per setting and a much smaller training budget than prior work
node error rates remained high and no listening test was reported

code_artifact_cards.title: RelFx public project repository availability audit
findings: the paper says source code is available at the project site
the visible public repository contains only index.html and an audio demo directory
no model source training code README lockfile or license file is visible
the public artifact is currently a demo site and does not support independent method reproduction

code_artifact_cards.title: WildFX repository availability audit
findings: Python source Docker/devcontainer setup sample metadata and two test modules are public
requirements are version-pinned including CPU-only torch wheels for the declared platforms
README treats nonzero exit partial batches and missing outputs as errors and adds a default three-second tail for delay echo and reverb layers
no repository license file or GitHub license identification is visible
REAPER plugin and source-dataset licenses remain separate prerequisites and were not exercised

knowledge_cards.claim: an ordered pair can represent the relative effect change even when neither member is truly dry
reference pairing must preserve musical section context because cross-section content differences can dominate effect differences
effect retrieval accuracy is not a substitute for style-transfer fit and can improve while transfer worsens
multi-resolution STFT loss measures signal fit but not musical preference production quality or preserved role
a mixture-level relative effect representation does not identify which source inside the mix should change
unseen processor order and real production chains require explicit out-of-distribution validation
a paper's source-code claim must be checked against the actual repository contents and license
graph labels must preserve processor order routing edge type sidechain role and linear gain to permit reconstruction
successful plugin loading does not establish non-silent finite correctly routed or musically valid output
headless DAW automation needs explicit error detection rendered-output validation and watchdog recovery
a constrained layered graph decomposition must be tested for render equivalence to the intended routing
single-run graph-estimation results on a five-plugin inventory are initial pipeline validation not a production-capability certificate
